title: Why Does Japan Have So Many Commemorative Days
paragraphs: If you look at a Japanese calendar closely, you may notice that almost every day seems to celebrate something. There are days for cats, days for married couples and even days for snacks. So why does Japan have so many commemorative days?

Part of the answer is official holidays. Japan has around 16 national holidays each year, which is a high number compared to many other countries. Some of them remember important events in history. For example, Constitution Memorial Day on May 3 marks the day Japan's postwar constitution came into effect.

However, most of Japan's special days are not official holidays at all. They are "kinenbi," or anniversary days, and many of them are created by companies, groups and even individuals. Since 1991, an organization called the Japan Anniversary Association has kept an official list of these days. People who want to create a new one can apply to have it registered.

Many of these days are chosen because of wordplay. In Japanese, numbers can be read in different ways, and their sounds can be combined to make words. This is called "goroawase." For instance, November 22, or 11/22, can be read as "ii fufu," which means "good married couple." That is why November 22 is known as Good Couple Day. February 22 is Cat Day, because the number two can sound like "nyan," the sound a cat makes in Japanese.

Other days are chosen because of how numbers look. November 11, or 11/11, is Pocky Day, because the four ones look like the popular thin chocolate snack sticks. The day was started in 1999 by the company that makes Pocky.

As you might guess, many of these days are a form of marketing. They give businesses a fun reason to promote their products and encourage people to buy them. So the next time you see a strange celebration on a Japanese calendar, there may be a company behind it.
